reuse.why: Consolidates the averaging actions into setMonthAverage but re-inlines the average/sign logic of the existing setNMonthAvg instead of calling it, and leaves copyPreviousMonth on a separate TS predicate.

duplication.why: The eligibility rule (hidden, group hidden, saved template) is written twice, once in SQL in getMonthActionCategories and once in isEligibleForMonthAction, and setMonthAverage duplicates setNMonthAvg's average-and-flip logic.

placement.why: All logic stays in budget/actions.ts next to the actions it serves, which matches the tree's layering.

scope.why: Focused on month-wide actions plus a test; it also folds the 3/6/12 month averages into one function, a reasonable but extra refactor, and leaves an unused BudgetCategory-related goal_def type on BudgetData.

maintainability.why: Two differently-shaped definitions of the same rule (SQL with empty-string check vs JS truthiness) can drift; a future rule change must be made in both.

bypasses_abstraction.where: setMonthAverage re-implements setNMonthAvg (getCategoryAverage + sign flip + setBudget) instead of calling it for set6MonthAvg/set12MonthAvg, which previously did.

disguised_duplication.where: The skip rule appears as a SQL WHERE clause in getMonthActionCategories and as isEligibleForMonthAction used only by copyPreviousMonth; setMonthAverage reshapes setNMonthAvg's body inline.

one_place.where: Rule lives both in getMonthActionCategories SQL (setZero, averages) and isEligibleForMonthAction (copyPreviousMonth).
